pr.title: Reduce false positives of tail-expr-drop-order from consumed values (attempt #2)
pr.description:
r? @nikomatsakis 

Tracked by #123739.

Related to #129864 but not replacing, yet.

Related to #130836.

This is an implementation of the approach suggested in the [Zulip stream](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/213817-t-lang/topic/temporary.20drop.20order.20changes). A new MIR statement `BackwardsIncompatibleDrop` is added to the MIR syntax. The lint now works by inspecting possibly live move paths before at the `BackwardsIncompatibleDrop` location and the actual drop under the current edition, which should be one before Edition 2024 in practice.

pr.author: dingxiangfei2009

analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, `tail_expr_drop_order` was an HIR late lint (`TailExprDropOrder`) that walked blocks and tail expressions. Its helper `expr_generates_nonlocal_droppy_value` returned false only when the expression eventually pointed into a local, then otherwise flagged the expression type whenever `has_significant_drop` was true. It did not consult MIR move/initialization state, so a droppy temporary that was actually consumed by the tail expression (return tuple, struct constructor, explicit move, parameter, closure capture) was still reported as reordered. MIR passes had no marker statement to carry this lint information.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historical over-approximation: flag every significant-drop tail temporary whenever any significant-drop local exists, even when the value is consumed into the return value, moved into a constructor, explicitly dropped/moved before the tail, or is a parameter/closure capture. For the pass-integration side, the analogous incorrect transformation is to treat `BackwardIncompatibleDropHint` as having no Place use (or to rename locals without remapping its Place), allowing SimplifyLocals to remove/rename a local that the marker still references; the fix instead records the marker in MIR, has the lint only report drops actually reachable between the marker and the real drop, and has local-usage/remapping passes preserve the marker's Place.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust functions and closures compiled under edition 2021 or earlier, containing significant-drop locals/temporaries, especially where the droppy tail temporary is (a) part of the returned tuple, (b) moved into a struct constructor, (c) explicitly moved/dropped before the tail, (d) a function parameter, (e) a by-value closure capture, (f) an async future/local, or (g) a generic or ADT value. Also MIR bodies containing `StatementKind::BackwardIncompatibleDropHint { place, reason }` while optimization passes run.
analysis.summary: Adding a semantically inert MIR marker statement requires coordinated pass handling: all MIR analyses/codegen must treat it as a no-op, while local-usage/remapping passes must keep its Place live and rewrite its Local. The PR also replaces an HIR over-approximation with a MIR maybe-initialized drop-reachability lint to avoid false positives for consumed/moved/parameter/closure-capture values.
analysis.trigger: MIR contains a new `StatementKind::BackwardIncompatibleDropHint { place, reason }` generated at a temporary's backwards-incompatible drop location, and both the tail-expr-drop-order lint and ordinary MIR optimization/validation passes run over that body.
preconditions: The marker is explicitly specified as semantically equivalent to `Nop`; codegen, MIRI, const-eval, borrowck, coverage, coroutine, and dataflow consumers must ignore it.
The marker carries a `Box<Place>` and therefore references a local that must remain valid through optimization.
SimplifyLocals' `UsedLocals` and `remove_unused_definitions_helper` must count the marker's place as a use, and its `LocalUpdater` must remap the marker's local index.
Validator's CFG checker and type checker must accept the variant as a no-op rather than reject it or fall into an unsupported-statement path.
The lint consumes the marker after `mir_promoted` is available; for the drop-reachability analysis, `MaybeInitializedPlaces` must be consulted so only drops that are actually in effect are counted.
pitfalls: Do not treat the marker as an actual drop or control-flow terminator; it is a no-op for borrowck, const-eval, codegen, coverage, coroutine analysis, and dataflow.

Do not delete the marker statement or its local just because the local has no other uses; the lint consumer relies on the marker, and deleting the local without deleting/rewriting the marker leaves invalid MIR.
When remapping locals, update the marker's `place.local`; otherwise local renumbering leaves a stale local index.
Early MIR still contains `Drop` terminators that drop elaboration may remove, so consulting `MaybeInitializedPlaces` before the primary effect is necessary to avoid counting unreachable drops.
Exclude `_0`, the closure capture-struct local, descendants of BID places, and types with no significant destructor when computing the set of reordered observers.
`ChunkedBitSet::subtract` and `intersect` were previously `unimplemented!`; the lint uses them, so domain sizes must match and the cached chunk counts must be maintained after mutation.
analysis.testStrategy: Use `tests/ui/drop/lint-tail-expr-drop-order.rs` under edition 2021 with `#![deny(tail_expr_drop_order)]`: positive cases (nested block, generic, ADT, async future, transient drops) must lint with the new message, while consumed/moved/parameter/closure-capture cases must not. Keep an edition-2024 gated test that verifies the migration lint does not fire. For the pass integration, add MIR/opt tests that run SimplifyLocals and Validator on a body containing `BackwardIncompatibleDropHint` and check that the marked local survives/remaps and that all MIR consumers accept the statement; assert codegen/const-eval treat it as a no-op. No compiler was built and no execution/reproduction was performed here.
evidence: +    /// This is semantically equivalent to `Nop`, so codegen and MIRI should interpret this
+    /// The only use case of this statement is for linting in MIR to detect temporary lifetime
+    // Should not lint because `LoudDropper` is consumed by the return value
+    // Should not lint because `x` is not live
+    // ^ closure captures like `x` are always dropped last by contract
